Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): invalidate preprocessor program queries when entry points change
Issues.Body:
Queries that read the compilation root list (`ProgramFiles`, and through it `ComponentMapping`, the NgModule scope registry and local-compilation extra imports) did not record that read as a dependency. Changes were instead covered by unconditionally evicting `ProgramFiles` whenever an already-analyzed file changed. A newly created file was never interned, so adding one returned early without that eviction: the root list was refreshed from the tsconfig, but program-level results computed before the file existed kept being served, e.g. a new NgModule's declarations were never picked up.

The root list is now a recorded query input. Queries that read it depend on a dedicated `ROOTS_FILE_ID`, and replacing the roots evicts exactly those queries, and everything derived from them, through the existing reverse index. The unconditional `ProgramFiles` eviction is no longer needed.

Refreshing the roots from the tsconfig after file updates now goes through `Analyzer::replace_entrypoints`, evicting nothing when the roots are unchanged and including any paths invalidated by root changes in the results of `updateFileContent` and `invalidateFiles`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(compiler-cli): invalidate preprocessor program queries when entry points change" (#71570)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): preserve isolated NgModule imports in emitDeclarationOnly mode
Issues.Body: Includes `isolatedImports` in `R3NgModuleMetadataKind.Isolated` when compiling under `emitDeclarationOnly` so `ɵɵNgModuleDeclaration` preserves its imports tuple type argument, and excludes namespace member expressions from isolated `NgModule` references.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): preserve isolated NgModule imports in emitDeclarationOnly mode" (#71583)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): always validate component hostDirectives and poison on error
Issues.Body: Runs `hostDirectives` resolution and validation on `@Component` declarations unconditionally (including when standalone `imports` have errors or when a non-standalone component is not declared in any `NgModule`), and marks declarations with invalid `hostDirectives` as poisoned so template type-checking is skipped unless `usePoisonedData` is enabled.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): always validate component hostDirectives and poison on error" (#71582)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): resolve @Input transform first-parameter types in coercion members
Issues.Body: Resolves concrete first-parameter types for same-file and imported named transform functions in `static ngAcceptInputType_*` coercion members when the parameter type is emittable, and emits `unknown` for zero-parameter inline and named transform functions.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): resolve @Input transform first-parameter types in coercion members" (#71581)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): emit ɵsetClassMetadata outside class when custom decorators exist
Issues.Body:
When a class has non-Angular class decorators alongside an Angular decorator, emitting `ɵsetClassMetadata` inside a `static { ... }` initializer block causes TypeScript's `__esDecorate` / `__decorate` helper to pass the replacement class returned by the custom decorator rather than the original class declaration.

This change tracks `hasNonAngularClassDecorators` on `ClassMetadata` and emits the `ɵsetClassMetadata` IIFE statement after the class declaration when non-Angular class decorators are present.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): emit ɵsetClassMetadata outside class when custom decorators exist" (#71580)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): downlevel jit: true Angular member and parameter decorators
Issues.Body:
When compiling a `@Component` or `@Directive` with `jit: true`, Angular constructor parameter decorators and identifier-named Angular member decorators must be stripped from the class and downleveled into `static ctorParameters` and `static propDecorators`, matching `ngtsc`.

This change preserves class-level decorators, non-Angular decorators, and string-literal-named member decorators on the class declaration, and skips decorator stripping and static property synthesis when `emitDeclarationOnly` is enabled.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): downlevel jit: true Angular member and parameter decorators" (#71579)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): emit ɵsetClassMetadata propDecorators in member declaration order
Issues.Body:
Previously, `buildPropDecoratorsExpr` in the preprocessor grouped `propDecorators` entries by category (decorated members first, followed by signal inputs, signal outputs, and signal queries) rather than class member declaration order.

This change records `memberSpan` on `DecoratedMemberMetadata` and sorts `propDecorators` entries by their source offset to match `ngtsc`'s declaration-order emission.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): emit ɵsetClassMetadata propDecorators in member declaration order" (#71578)

## What is the current behavior?

Since #71504, adev drives the Router through the platform Navigation API
(`withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`) whenever `window.navigation` is available.

Firefox versions prior to 159 have a bug in their Navigation API implementation (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2077448) that crashes the tab on fragment navigations. On angular.dev this happens whenever a visitor uses the "On this page" menu, clicks a heading, or opens a URL with a hash such as

Issue Number: #71567

## What is the new behavior?

`withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()` is skipped when the user agent is Firefox with a major version lower than 159. Those browsers fall back to the history-based `Location`, as they did before #71504. All other browsers, and Firefox 159+, keep the Navigation API integration.

The version check lives in an exported `hasBrokenPlatformNavigation(userAgent)` helper with unit tests. It is a temporary workaround, marked with a TODO to be removed once Firefox < 159 is no longer in use.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): disallow event attributes and sanitize bindings with colon prefixes
Issues.Body:
Previously, attribute bindings using a leading colon (such as `[attr.:onclick]` or `[attr.:href]`) bypassed security checks because the colon was stripped by `mergeNsAndName` only after attribute validation and security context resolution had already taken place. As a result, `[attr.:onclick]` evaded event attribute validation and `[attr.:href]` bypassed URL sanitization.

This change ensures that:
1. Event attribute validation (`validateAttribute`) and property validation (`validateProperty`) extract the local name when colons or namespace prefixes are present, properly disallowing bindings like `:onclick` or `svg:onclick`.
2. Attribute bindings with leading colons or namespaces are validated properly in template transform and host bindings verification.
3. Security context resolution strips any leading colon so attributes like `:href` or `:src` receive the appropriate sanitizer.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): disallow event attributes and sanitize bindings with colon prefixes" (#71575)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): do not scope nested `&` selectors that refer to the host

## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Since nested rules are scoped (#69885), a compound selector that starts with `&` inside `:host` gets the content attribute too:

```css
:host {
  &.md { width: 70px; }
  &:hover, &[disabled] { color: red; }
}
```

becomes

```css
[_nghost-c1] {
  &.md[_ngcontent-c1] { width: 70px; }
  &[_ngcontent-c1]:hover, &[disabled][_ngcontent-c1] { color: red; }
}
```

The host element does not have its own content attribute, so none of these rules match anymore. The same happens under `:host(.foo)` and `:host-context(.dark)`, inside at-rules such as `@media` nested in `:host`, and for `&` nested in another `&` rule under `:host`.

Issue Number: #71050

## What is the new behavior?

When the parent rule matches the host element, a compound selector that starts with `&` is left as it is (`[_nghost-c1] { &.md {} }`), so it matches the same elements as the flat form `:host.md`. Everything else is scoped as before:

- descendants and siblings: `& .child` becomes `& .child[_ngcontent-c1]`
- `&` under a rule whose subject is an element of the template, such as `:host .child { &.active {} }`: unchanged
- `&` inside `@scope` nested in `:host`, where `&` refers to the scoping root: unchanged
- rules without `:host`, such as `.parent { &.modifier {} }`: unchanged

On `&:is(...)`: the review of #71152 suggested scoping the selectors inside `:is()`, for example `&:is(.foo[_ngcontent-c1], .bar[_ngcontent-c1] > .baz[_ngcontent-c1])`. Under `:host` those selectors describe the host element itself (`.foo`) or its ancestors (`.bar`). Neither is part of the component's template, so neither has the content attribute, and such a rule could never match. This PR leaves them unscoped, which is what `:host:is(.foo, .bar > .baz)` gives today (`[_nghost-c1]:is(.foo, .bar > .baz)`). On main the nested form is `&[_ngcontent-c1]:is(.foo, .bar > .baz)`, which does not scope the inner selectors either. A spec covers both forms.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

I ran the `shadow_css` specs with jasmine (bundled with esbuild, not through Bazel): 150 pass. Four of the six new specs fail without the fix; the other two (`@scope` and `:host .child`) pin output that does not change. Both files type-check with TypeScript 6.0.3 in strict mode and are formatted with prettier 3.9.10.

Issues.Title: perf(core): avoid unnecessary aborts and reuse abort reason during resource teardown
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [x] Other... Please describe: Performance optimization

## What is the current behavior?

When tearing down a view tree containing resources (e.g. during route navigation), `ResourceImpl.destroy()` invokes `abortInProgressLoad()`, calling `pendingController.abort()` without arguments.

This leads to significant teardown latency due to two factors:
1. Per the WHATWG DOM spec, calling `abort()` with no reason instantiates a new `"AbortError"` `DOMException`. In V8/Chromium, `DOMException` construction triggers `v8::Exception::CaptureStackTrace()`. The cost of walking execution stack frames scales linearly with call stack depth (~140 µs per call at depth 300 on throttled CPUs). When destroying dozens of resources in deep view trees, this adds 20–40ms of main thread blockage.
2. `ResourceImpl` retains its `pendingController` even after a one-shot (non-streaming) loader has settled (resolved or errored). When the component is eventually destroyed, `abort()` is executed on controllers whose operations finished long ago.

Issue Number: #71422

## What is the new behavior?

1. **Reused Abort Reason**:
   `abortInProgressLoad()` now passes a shared, lazily-initialized `DOMException('The operation was aborted.', 'AbortError')`. Passing an existing `DOMException` prevents V8 from capturing a fresh call stack on every call while preserving complete Web API and consumer compatibility (`err.name === 'AbortError'`, `err instanceof DOMException`).
2. **Clear Pending Controller on Completion**:
   For non-streaming resources (`PromiseResourceOptions`), once the loader promise settles (in `finally`), `pendingController` is cleared if it belongs to that settled load. When the resource is destroyed later, teardown does not perform unnecessary abort work or event dispatch. Streaming resources (like `rxResource` or `StreamingResourceOptions`) retain their controller so active subscriptions and streams continue to be cleanly aborted on destroy.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Draft PR proposing the two-pronged optimization discussed in #71422 and #71423.

- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #34514

The server build emits two complete copies of domino: `polyfills.server.mjs` bundles it via `@angular/platform-server/init`, and `main.server.mjs` bundles it again via `@angular/platform-server`. The two bundles are separate esbuild contexts, so the shared `third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` module is inlined into each, and both are evaluated at runtime (`main.server.mjs` imports `./polyfills.server.mjs` first).

Because the two copies are distinct class hierarchies, DOM globals captured at module-evaluation time (the scenario `init` exists for) do not match the classes the platform renders with:

```ts
const Captured = HTMLElement;              // polyfills.server.mjs copy
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof Captured; // false: body is from the main.server.mjs copy
```

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the new behavior that. -->

The server polyfills bundle re-exports the domino module it already contains, and the main server bundle redirects the `@angular/platform-server` import of `../third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` to that export. `./polyfills.server.mjs` is already in `SERVER_GENERATED_EXTERNALS` and imported first by every server bundle, so the evaluation order is unchanged.

The polyfills bundle has to stay a separate, externally imported file: with code splitting, a side-effect import at the top of the `main.server` entry is inlined into the entry while shared chunks are hoisted above it, so moving the `init` import there would run it after shared application chunks. Sharing the copy avoids that.

On the default `ng new --ssr` app (Angular CLI 22.2.4, Node 26.8.1):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bundled-domino.mjs` in `main.server.mjs` | yes | no |
| `main.server.mjs` (production) | 537 kB | 301 kB |
| Retained V8 heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,831 KB |
| `body instanceof capturedHTMLElement` | false | true |
| SSR response | 200, 22,064 B | 200, 22,064 B |

Covered: `outputMode: 'server'`, the legacy `ssr` + `prerender` path (same esbuild context and banner), `platform: 'neutral'`, prerendering, and the dev server when bundling. When packages are external (`ng serve` prebundling) nothing changes; Node's module cache already shares one copy there. If `@angular/platform-server` is not installed, is external, or has an unexpected layout, both sides fall back to today's behavior.

Reproduction with the measurement harness and the `instanceof` probe: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

`@angular/platform-server/init` is still added to every server build. Making that optional (and the server polyfills list user-controllable in general) is a separate request: #34515.

Issues.Title: Server polyfills are not user-controllable: no way to opt out of `@angular/platform-server/init` or add server-only polyfills
Issues.Body:
### Command

build, serve

### Description

`@angular/build:application` derives the server polyfills list entirely on its own and offers no option to change it. In `createServerPolyfillBundleOptions` ([application-code-bundle.ts#L164-L184](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L164-L184)):

- `zone.js/node` (or `zone.js` on `platform: 'neutral'`) is added when the browser `polyfills` list contains `zone.js`,
- `@angular/localize/init` is added when the browser list contains it,
- `@angular/platform-server/init` is **always** added.

So the browser polyfills list is fully explicit, and the server polyfills list is fully implicit. Two concrete gaps follow from that:

#### 1. There is no opt-out of the `init` global patch

`@angular/platform-server/init` is a side-effectful module whose only job is `Object.assign(globalThis, domino.impl)` plus `globalThis.KeyboardEvent = domino.impl.Event`. The framework introduced it as something an app *may* import before bootstrap for code that touches DOM globals at module-evaluation time ([angular/angular#40559](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/40559)). Most apps do not need it: `platform-server` runs the identical shim itself in `DominoAdapter.makeCurrent()` → `setDomTypes()` on every platform init, so for everything that runs after bootstrap the `init` patch is redundant and is overwritten on the first render anyway.

Since v15 the CLI adds it to every server build with no way to say no. Evidence that people need the opt-out:

- The framework's own SSR benchmarks patch `@angular/build` to strip the `platform-server/init` import from `polyfills.server.mjs` (`modules/ssr-benchmarks/README.md` in angular/angular), and the `main.server.ts` there notes that `ɵENABLE_DOM_EMULATION` "won't prevent the monkey patching of DOM apis as this is introduced by the CLI".
- Anyone running the server bundle outside Node with a real DOM (the benchmark case, or `ENABLE_DOM_EMULATION: false`) gets Domino's classes forced onto `globalThis` regardless.
- Apps that want to keep `globalThis` clean on the server (no `HTMLElement`, `Node`, `Event`, … leaking into third-party code that feature-detects the environment with `typeof window`/`typeof HTMLElement`) have no option either.

Measured on a default `ng new --ssr` app (details in #34514): the `init` module costs ~235 kB on disk, ~1.1 MB of retained heap for the life of the process and ~7 ms of startup, while the `Object.assign` itself is negligible (~7 KB, 0.03 ms). Prerendered and SSR output are byte-identical with and without it.

#### 2. There is nowhere to put a server-only polyfill

The `ssr.platform` option's own description says *"Please note that this feature does not provide polyfills for Node.js modules."* With `platform: 'neutral'` (Cloudflare Workers and similar), users are expected to bring polyfills themselves, yet the only polyfills option feeds the browser bundle. Today a server-only polyfill has to be imported manually at the top of `main.server.ts`, where it runs after `zone.js` and `init` and after any shared chunks.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let `polyfills` take either the current array or a browser/server object, mirroring the existing `outputPath` shape (`string | { base, browser, server, media }`):

```jsonc
"polyfills": ["zone.js"]                                 // today, unchanged
"polyfills": {
  "browser": ["zone.js"],
  "server": ["zone.js/node", "@angular/platform-server/init"]
}
```

Semantics:

- **Array form keeps today's behaviour exactly**: `browser` = the array, `server` = derived as now (`zone.js/node`, localize, `init`). Non-breaking; no migration needed.
- **An explicit `server` list is the server polyfills list**, the same way the browser list already is: the builder adds nothing on top. To drop the `init` global patch, omit it. To keep today's output, list it. The `ng new` / `ssr` schematics can emit the explicit form so new projects see what they get.
- `isZonelessApp` is evaluated per list (browser list for the browser bundle, server list for the server bundle), so `zone.js` vs `zone.js/node` and the async/await support flags fall out naturally.
- `getEsBuildCommonPolyfillsOptions` and the `polyfills.server` bundle are unchanged; only the input list is. Normalization follows the existing `normalizeOptimization` / `normalizeSourceMaps` pattern (a small `normalizePolyfills` in `options.ts`, folding in the string-to-array shim that `browser-esbuild` still relies on).
- Consumers that read `options.polyfills` and would switch to `.browser` / `.server`: `application-code-bundle.ts` (browser bundle, server bundle, `isZonelessApp` checks), `execute-build.ts` (top-level-await hint), `dev-server/vite/index.ts` (`es2016` target), and `browser-esbuild`'s string handling.

This solves both gaps with one option and no new concept: server polyfills become as explicit as browser polyfills.

I am happy to implement this and open the PR once the shape is agreed; the single-copy fix in #34516 is independent of it and already covers the duplicate.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

**A boolean under `ssr`**, next to `ssr.platform`, which already shapes the server polyfill list (`zone.js` vs `zone.js/node`), the `createRequire` banner and the `xhr2` external:

```jsonc
"ssr": { "entry": "src/server.ts", "platform": "node", "domShims": false }
```

One `if` around line 184. It only addresses gap 1, and the name needs care so it is not confused with the framework's private `ɵENABLE_DOM_EMULATION`, which controls the adapter and does not affect the global shims.

**Leaving it manual**: users who want `init` could import it in `main.server.ts` as the v12 schematic did. That would be a breaking change for apps that rely on the implicit import, and it still leaves gap 2.

**Not an alternative, but related**: the same unconditional `init` import is also why the server build currently ships two copies of Domino (#34514). That has a bundling-level fix that does not need this option; this request is about control, not about the duplicate.

### Anything else relevant?

- No spec or e2e currently asserts anything about `polyfills.server.mjs`, `zone.js/node` or `@angular/platform-server/init`; `tests/options/polyfills_spec.ts` only covers `dist/browser/polyfills.js`. Either solution should add a server polyfills spec.
- The webpack server builder only adds `init` when `@angular/platform-server` is installed (`isPackageInstalled` in `webpack/configs/common.ts`); the esbuild path has no equivalent guard.
- Repro and measurements: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

Issues.Title: Server build bundles two copies of Domino, so DOM globals from `init` and the `DominoAdapter` are different classes
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

Not a regression. The second copy appeared when the dedicated `polyfills.server` bundle was introduced in v17 and has been there since.

### Description

With `outputMode: 'server'` (the default `ng new --ssr` setup), `@angular/build:application` emits two complete copies of Domino into the server output, and both are evaluated in the same Node process:

| File | Brings in Domino via |
|---|---|
| `polyfills.server.mjs` | `@angular/platform-server/init`, pushed unconditionally in `createServerPolyfillBundleOptions` ([application-code-bundle.ts#L184](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L184)) |
| `main.server.mjs` | `@angular/platform-server` itself (`DominoAdapter`) |

The two bundles are separate esbuild contexts, so the `third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` module that both entry points import is inlined into each output. `main.server.mjs` starts with `import './polyfills.server.mjs'`, so both copies load.

#### The two copies are different class hierarchies

`platform-server` runs the same shim as `init` in `DominoAdapter.makeCurrent()` → `setDomTypes()` during `PLATFORM_INITIALIZER`, using *its* copy. So on the first render every global that `init` set is overwritten by the second copy. Any code that captured a DOM class at module-evaluation time, which is exactly the scenario `init` exists to support, then holds a class from the other hierarchy:

```ts
// top of some module (e.g. a library doing `class Foo extends HTMLElement`)
const Captured = HTMLElement;                   // Domino copy #1, from polyfills.server.mjs

// later, during rendering
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof Captured;      // false  (body is from copy #2)
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof HTMLElement;   // true   (global was overwritten)
Captured === HTMLElement;                       // false
```

#### Measured cost of the second copy

Default `ng new --ssr` app, Angular CLI 22.2.4, `@angular/build` 22.2.4, `@angular/platform-server` 22.2.3, Node 26.8.1. "Without" is the same build with `@angular/platform-server/init` removed from the server polyfills and nothing else changed. Memory is the median over 11 fresh processes per variant, forced GC before each snapshot, after serving 50 SSR requests.

| | With `init` (default) | Without | Cost of the extra copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `polyfills.server.mjs` on disk | 235.58 kB | 128 B | **235 kB** |
| Retained V8 heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,739 KB | **~1.1 MB** |
| Retained V8 heap after 50 requests | 12,477 KB | 11,342 KB | **~1.1 MB** (does not grow) |
| Import time of `polyfills.server.mjs` | ~7.5 ms | ~0.6 ms | **~7 ms** startup |
| Prerendered / SSR HTML | identical | identical | — |

The 1.1 MB is permanent: the ESM module namespace keeps every Domino function and prototype reachable for the lifetime of the process. From a heap-snapshot diff it is roughly 350 KB compiled code and function metadata, 340 KB retained source strings, 200 KB prototype and lookup tables, 110 KB function objects, and V8 internals for the rest. The `Object.assign(globalThis, domino.impl)` itself is negligible (95 properties, ~7 KB, 0.03 ms); the cost is the second module evaluation.

To be clear about scale: in a fresh default app the duplicate is about 30% of the retained heap after loading the server bundles and about 2% of process RSS once requests are served. Small in absolute terms, but pure overhead on every SSR deployment, and the `instanceof` inconsistency above comes with it.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.2.4 new repro --ssr --defaults
cd repro
npx ng build --configuration development   # keeps esbuild's module markers
grep -n "^// node_modules/@angular/platform-server" dist/repro/server/*.mjs
```

Actual:

```
main.server.mjs:36143:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs
main.server.mjs:52859:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/_server-chunk.mjs
main.server.mjs:53402:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/platform-server.mjs
polyfills.server.mjs:4:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs
polyfills.server.mjs:16720:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/init.mjs
```

Expected: `bundled-domino.mjs` appears once across the server output.

Full repro with the memory-measurement harness and the `instanceof` probe: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

### Exception or Error

```
(none; the build succeeds)
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.4
Node.js           : 26.8.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0

@angular/build            22.2.4
@angular/core             22.2.3
@angular/platform-server  22.2.3
@angular/ssr              22.2.4
```

### Anything else relevant?

#### Proposed fix (no API change), PR to follow

The polyfills bundle has to stay a separate, externally imported file: it is the only thing that guarantees `zone.js` and `init` evaluate before application code. (With code splitting, a side-effect import at the top of the `main.server` entry is inlined into the entry file while shared chunks are hoisted above it, so moving the `init` import there runs it *after* shared app chunks.) So the fix shares the copy rather than moving it:

- `polyfills.server.mjs` additionally re-exports the Domino module it already bundles via `init`.
- The main server bundle redirects `@angular/platform-server`'s `../third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` import to that export. `./polyfills.server.mjs` is already in `SERVER_GENERATED_EXTERNALS`, so this becomes a plain external import.

Verified on the repro above with the patched builder:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bundled-domino.mjs` in `main.server.mjs` | yes | no |
| `main.server.mjs` (production) | 537 kB | 301 kB |
| Retained heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,831 KB |
| `body instanceof capturedHTMLElement` / `captured === HTMLElement` | false / false | true / true |
| SSR response | 200, 22,064 B | 200, 22,064 B |

It covers `outputMode: 'server'`, the legacy `ssr` + `prerender` path (same esbuild context, same banner), `platform: 'neutral'`, prerendering, and the dev server when bundling. When packages are external (`ng serve` prebundling) nothing changes, and Node's module cache already shares one copy there. The change comes with a spec under `builders/application/tests/behavior/`; today no spec or e2e asserts anything about `polyfills.server.mjs`.

#### Related

This fix keeps `@angular/platform-server/init` in every server build. Whether it should be there at all, and the lack of any user control over the server polyfills list, is a separate request: #34515.

<details>
<summary>How the duplicate came about</summary>

- **angular/angular#40559 (v12, 2021)** — `@angular/platform-server/init` created so DOM globals are available *before* platform init.
- **angular-cli `1199205bc` (v12)** — `universal` schematic adds the import to `main.server.ts`.
- **angular-cli `979bce45e` (v15)** — webpack server builder auto-adds it, removing the schematic import. `f143171fd` gates it on `@angular/platform-server` being installed (#24188).
- **angular-cli `095f5aba6` / `7defb3635` (v16)** — esbuild server bundling imports it in the virtual `main.server` entry; one copy.
- **angular-cli `886cb3167` (v17)** — a separate `polyfills.server` bundle is created to control zone.js flag ordering for cleaner stack traces. `init` moves into it with the other server polyfills. This is where the second copy starts; the commit is about zone.js and does not mention it.
- **angular/angular#52342 (v17)** — the shared `setDomTypes` import between `init` and `platform-server` is removed so the CLI can skip the JS transformer on the polyfills bundle (angular-cli#26113). After this the two entry points share no module, which guarantees two copies when bundled separately.

So the duplicate was never a deliberate choice; it fell out of two independent build-performance changes.

</details>

- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`trust-proxy-headers` migration collects only `server` option of `build` target
In workspace created by `ng new --ssr` on 21 that option is `src/main.server.ts`, and `new AngularNodeAppEngine()` is in `src/server.ts`, which is set in `ssr.entry`

So `ng update` from 21 prints `Migration completed (No changes made)` for this migration and `src/server.ts` keeps `new AngularNodeAppEngine()` without options
On 21 undefined `trustProxyHeaders` trusted `x-forwarded-host` and `x-forwarded-proto`, on 22 it trusts nothing (#32911), so after update default SSR app stops trusting these headers and only logs warning when they arrive, which is exactly what migration was ment to avoid

Existing spec cases pass only because test workspace has `server: '/server.ts'`, `ng new` does not create that layout

## What is the new behavior?

Migration also collects `ssr.entry` file from `build` target options and configurations, `server` is still collected for other layouts
On default SSR workspace `src/server.ts` gets TODO comment and `trustProxyHeaders: ['x-forwarded-host', 'x-forwarded-proto']`, `src/main.server.ts` is left as is

New case in `migration_spec.ts` uses real layout (`server: 'src/main.server.ts'`, `ssr.entry: 'src/server.ts'`), it fails on main

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Workspaces that already went to 22 can run it again once they are on release with this fix:

```
ng update @angular/cli --name trust-proxy-headers
```

Issues.Title: ssr: string redirectTo drops trailing slash in query and fragment
Issues.Body:
### Command

build, serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

none, same baseHref join is there since 19.0.0

### Description

String `redirectTo` loses trailing `/` of query or fragment in `Location`: `'/login?next=/a/'` gives `/login?next=/a` and `'/login#section/'` gives `/login#section`. Same with `X-Forwarded-Prefix` and with base href `/base/`, on 22.2.4 and on main snapshot `22.3.0-next.3+sha-928169a`

Function redirect with same target keeps it (`/login?next=%2Fa%2F` and `/login#section/`) since router serializes it, so same target gives diffrent `Location` depending only on how redirect is written

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `npx -p @angular/cli@latest ng new repro --ssr --defaults --skip-git`
2. `src/app/app.routes.ts`:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

@Component({ template: 'login' })
class Login {}

export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: 'login', component: Login },
  { path: 'old', redirectTo: '/login?next=/a/' },
  { path: 'old-hash', redirectTo: '/login#section/' },
  { path: 'old-fn', redirectTo: () => '/login?next=/a/' },
  { path: 'old-fn-hash', redirectTo: () => '/login#section/' },
];
```

3. `src/app/app.routes.server.ts`: `[{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }]` so function redirects go through render
4. `ng build` then `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost NG_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=x-forwarded-prefix node dist/repro/server/server.mjs`
5. curl:

```text
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old | grep -i '^location'
location: /login?next=/a
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /login#section
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-fn | grep -i '^location'
location: /login?next=%2Fa%2F
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-fn-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /login#section/
$ curl -si -H 'X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app' localhost:4000/old | grep -i '^location'
location: /app/login?next=/a
$ curl -si -H 'X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app' localhost:4000/old-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /app/login#section
```

With `ng build --base-href /base/` it's `/base/login?next=/a` and `/base/login#section`. Slash is gone already at build time, `dist/repro/server/angular-app-manifest.mjs` has `"redirectTo": "/login?next=/a"`

Expected: `/login?next=/a/` and `/login#section/`, with `/app` or `/base` in front when set

Actual: trailing slash of query and fragment is gone

### Exception or Error

```text
none, only Location header is wrong
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.4
Angular           : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.16.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.13.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.4           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.4           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-server  │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/ssr              │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.4           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
│ vitest                    │ 5.0.5             │ ^5.0.0            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘

same output with @angular/ssr 22.3.0-next.3+sha-928169a from angular-ssr-builds
```

### Anything else relevant?

`joinUrlParts` trims trailing `/` of every part, and two places still pass it whole target with query and fragment: [`joinUrlParts(baseHref, metadata.redirectTo)`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/928169a68b522b8f38334ee2626687704495e5ec/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts#L900) in `extractRoutesAndCreateRouteTree` and [prefix join](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/928169a68b522b8f38334ee2626687704495e5ec/packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts#L170-L173) in `AngularServerApp.handle`

[#34467](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/34467) description says `joinUrlParts` is applied only to path portion when prepending `baseHref` or `X-Forwarded-Prefix` so trailing slashes in query or fragment are preserved, but both joins above still take whole target. If that's not intended I can send PR that splits off query and fragment first, like `resolveRedirectTo` does

Issues.Body: In an application with SSR enabled, `ng g web-worker app` appends the worker creation snippet to `app.config.server.ts` instead of the component file. The sibling file exclusion pattern is end-anchored, so `app.config.server.ts` and `app.routes.server.ts` end in `server.ts` rather than `config.ts`/`routes.ts` and are not excluded, and the alphabetical sort places `app.config.server.ts` before `app.ts`. Issues.Title: 22.3.0-next build library change input entries source and output structure
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Description

This is meant as early feedback for 22.3.0-next to improve the interface before the final version is release as this is be a breaking change to the existing solution.

#### input entries source
The current implementation requires developers to add the entry points to package.json exports field.
If the package should now be publish the export will point to the .ts files instead of the actual compiled ones.

There are workaround for this for example
```yaml
# deploy the dist folder of the angular wrapper that was created by ng-packgr
# npm no longer respects publishConfig.directory => physically replace the original folder with the built dist folder.

script:
    - mv packages/angular-library/dist /tmp/ng-dist
    - rm -rf packages/angular-library
    - mkdir -p packages/angular-library
    - cp -a /tmp/ng-dist/. packages/angular-library
```

#### output structure
currently the output structure is similar to ng-packagr:

- dist
  - fesm2022
    - my-component.mjs
  - my-component
    - package.json
  - .npmignore
  - package.json

this is quite verbose and uses multiple package.json which are only used for development

the tsconfig will also need to be altered to point to the correct path:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "angular-library/*": ["../angular-library/dist/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Describe the solution you'd like

#### input entries source

instead of polluting the package.json an `exports` option could be added to angular.json build target instead.

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@angular/cli/lib/config/schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "projects": {
    "angular-library": {
      "projectType": "library",
      "root": ".",
      "sourceRoot": "src",
      "architect": {
        "build": {
          "builder": "@angular/build:library",
          "options": {
            "exports": {
               ".": "src/barrel-file.ts",
               "./my-component": "src/lib/my-component.ts"
             }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### output structure

instead of writing multiple package.json the entry points can be directly written to the package.json exports field. This will result in a flat dist folder layout and no more need to configure tsconfig.

- dist
  - my-component.mjs

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): avoid expanding directory patterns in asset globs
Issues.Body:
Previously, when an asset entry specified a directory pattern in `glob` (such as `glob: 'sub/'` or `glob: 'sub'`), its behavior differed depending on whether `ignore` was present:
- Without `ignore`, the static single-file fast-path checked `stats.isFile()` and returned no files.
- With `ignore`, `tinyglobby` ran with its default `expandDirectories: true` option and recursively matched all files in the directory.

This change disables `expandDirectories` for `glob` in `resolveAssets` while preserving directory expansion for `ignore` patterns via a shared `normalizeAssetIgnorePatterns` helper.

Issues.Title: build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout
Issues.Body:
This change restores `if: github.event.repository.fork == false` on `.github/workflows/assistant-to-the-branch-manager.yml` on the `22.2.x` branch per GHSS `pull_request_target` policy remediation (b/577107676).

Because 100% of pull requests in `angular/components` originate from forks (`only_allow_releasable_branches: true`) and `branch-manager` requires `context.eventName === 'pull_request_target'` along with `secrets.ANGULAR_ROBOT_PRIVATE_KEY` to set mergeability commit status, the previous `head.repo.fork == false` check caused all fork PR runs to be skipped. Restoring the base repository fork check ensures branch-manager triggers as intended on upstream PRs while preventing runs on external forks.

Additionally, `persist-credentials: false` is added to `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/google-internal-tests.yml` for defense-in-depth.

Clicks in components handeld via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 should work.

### Actual Behavior

Clicks in components handled via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 do not work.

Issues.Title: Feature (MatDialog): Add an option to prevent duplicate dialogs
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

Currently, Angular Material’s MatDialog allows the same component to be opened multiple times, resulting in multiple instances of the same dialog being displayed simultaneously.

In some applications, this behavior is undesirable. For example, repeated user interactions or multiple event emissions can accidentally open the same dialog more than once.

Developers must currently implement their own duplicate detection logic using MatDialog.openDialogs or MatDialog.getDialogById() before calling MatDialog.open().

Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a built-in option in MatDialogConfig to prevent duplicate instances of the same component from being opened.

For example:

this.dialog.open(MyDialogComponent, {
  preventDuplicates: true,
});

When this option is enabled, attempting to open a component that already has an open dialog could either:

* Return the existing MatDialogRef without creating another instance.
* Ignore the new request and keep the existing dialog open.

The exact behavior could be determined by the maintainers.

Ideally, duplicate detection would be scoped to the component type, with an option to customize the behavior if needed.

Benefits

* Avoids accidentally opening multiple instances of the same dialog.
* Reduces repetitive boilerplate across applications.
* Provides a consistent, framework-level solution.
* Keeps applications simpler and less error-prone.

Alternatives considered

Currently, developers can manually inspect openDialogs or use getDialogById() before opening a dialog. However, this requires additional application-level logic and does not provide a straightforward, reusable option for this common use case.

Would this feature be a good fit for Angular Material’s MatDialog API? I’d be happy to contribute a PR if the maintainers consider this approach appropriate.

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
When a checkbox or slide toggle is bound to a signal forms field whose schema uses `required()`, signal forms set the component's `required` input and also run the component's own validator. This resulted in two `required` errors, and the one from the component doesn't have the message from the schema, which hides it when using `getError('required')`.

These changes skip the component's `required` validation when it's bound to a signal forms field, since the schema already handles it.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33990)

Issues.Title: fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item
Issues.Body:
When a menu item opens an overlay, like a dialog, that focuses its content before the menu closes (e.g. when animations are disabled), the menu would restore focus to its trigger behind the overlay. These changes skip restoring focus when the menu is closed by a click and focus has moved into a different overlay. Focus is still restored if it's in another menu (e.g. when clicking an item in a sub-menu), in the overlay containing the trigger, or outside of any overlay.

Fixes #33967.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item" (#33989)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added
Issues.Body:
Updates the `SortedCollection` so it doesn't emit changes when a DOM node that's not a member of the collection is added. I also did some internal cleanup so we don't need to re-create the `Set` all the time and to keep a version counter.

Fixes #33976.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added" (#33996)

Issues.Title: fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
The checkbox has a custom required error in template/reactive forms. When it's used together with the signal forms interop, it was causing double `required` errors to show up. These changes skip the custom validation when signal forms are present.

Also fixes a similar issue with the slide toggle.

Fixes #33945.

Issues.Title: docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events
Issues.Body:
Adds a section to the scrolling overview that shows how to listen to scroll events with `cdkScrollable` and the `ScrollDispatcher`, along with a live example.

Fixes #9594 
The scrolling overview only had two short paragraphs about `cdkScrollable` and `ScrollDispatcher` and didn't show how to actually listen to scroll events. This adds:

- a section on `elementScrolled`, `scrolled` and `ancestorScrolled`, with a snippet
- a live example (`cdk-scrollable-overview`) that shows the scroll offset and scrolls back to the top
- a note that the events fire outside the Angular zone, so the view only updates if you use signals or `markForCheck`

### [`v12.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.15.0): pnpm 12.15

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.14.0...v12.15.0)

This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](https://pnpm.io/config-includes).

  A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`.

- Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity.

  ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  lockfile:
    integrityTarget: tar
  ```

- pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-lock.yaml` records the hash of each tar. Declare such a registry with `serverType: pnpr` in `registries` to keep tarball URLs out of the lockfile. See [Tar registries](https://pnpm.io/registries#tar-registries).

  pnpm now decodes the content coding of tarball downloads itself. It rejects a zstd response whose window is larger than 8 MiB.

  Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. It caps the bytes the files of one package may unpack to, 4 GiB by default.

- Registry revisions now always pin the hash of the uncompressed tar, the original included. pnpm records an original selected through the revision protocol, for example with a `+r0` specifier, as `revision: 0` in the lockfile and fetches it from the registry's digest route. pnpm checks a revision's tar whether the registry sends it as a tar, gzip, or zstd. Revision metadata must list revision 0 and mark the selected revision. pnpm rejects incomplete revision metadata with `ERR_PNPM_MALFORMED_METADATA`.

- pnpm now accepts zstd-compressed responses. Registries that serve zstd send package metadata in fewer bytes than with gzip, most of all the full metadata that settings such as `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` read.

- `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install` now use the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable as an upper bound for timestamps in `node_modules/.modules.yaml` and `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. With an equivalently prepared deploy target and an epoch no later than the timestamps that would otherwise be recorded, deploying the same project twice produces identical files [#​17171](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17171).

- `pnpm update --interactive` now highlights the row under the cursor in cyan while keeping the colors of its version changes.

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it.

- `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#​17142](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17142).

##### Resolving dependencies

- When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#​17084](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17084).

- When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#​17058](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17058).

- A package that lists the same dependency in `dependencies` and as an optional peer now gets the peer bound when a project adds a provider for it later. The lockfile now records every peer a package declares, including one its own dependency supplies [#​17056](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17056).

- `pnpm install --prod` and `pnpm deploy --prod` no longer drop a dependency that a package declares both as an optional peer and as its own dependency, when the package resolved it as its own dependency and a dev dependency provides the same package under another alias.

- `pnpm install` with an existing lockfile and a second `pnpm dedupe` now keep optional peer bindings that point into a dependency cycle or back into the dependent package. Before, the second run dropped the optional peer binding from the lockfile snapshot key.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now preserve own-dependency and peer-dependency bindings when reusing a lockfile whose peer suffixes were hashed by `peersSuffixMaxLength`.

  Upgrading a direct dependency in one workspace project now refreshes matching transitive pins in sibling projects during the same `pnpm install` pass.

- With `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot: false`, a workspace project no longer binds a peer to a version that only another project's dependencies provide. pnpm now auto-installs a version that satisfies the peer range for that project. Before, the project got a version outside the range, with no peer warning.

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, and `pnpm update` now reuse the lockfile's resolution for dependencies that take part in a dependency cycle, such as `mlly` and `pkg-types`. They re-resolved those packages and everything that depends on them from the registry before [pnpm/tasks#130](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/130).

- pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote. The install then linked a directory that does not exist, or failed if workspace packages were injected [#​17010](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17010).

- `pnpm install` now removes config dependencies that are no longer declared, including when the entire `configDependencies` setting is removed. Frozen installs reject a lockfile that still records removed config dependencies.

- `pnpm install --update-checksums` now re-resolves every locked package and records the integrity the registry reports now.

- `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now accept `gist:<id>` dependencies and GitHub Gist URLs, and install them from the gist's archive. `pnpm pkg fix` normalizes a `gist:` repository the way `npm pkg fix` does, `pnpm licenses` links a gist package to its gist page, and `pnpm sbom` reports the repository of a package whose `repository` field is a `gist:` shorthand.

- `pnpm add` now reads the package name correctly from a tarball URL under a registry URL that has a path, such as `https://example.com/npm/`, and installs a registry tarball URL with a malformed percent escape as a plain tarball URL. Before, the registry path became part of the name, so a scoped package failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME`.

- With `minimumReleaseAge` set, pnpm now revalidates a package's cached full metadata with a single ETag request so an unchanged registry answers with `304`, even when the registry does not list a publish time for every version. Previously, pnpm downloaded that metadata again whenever the cached copy was older than `minimumReleaseAge`. With `resolutionMode` set to `lowest-direct` or `time-based`, pnpm also reuses that metadata across every workspace project that depends on the package.

- When pnpm revalidates cached registry metadata, it now sends `If-Modified-Since` when the registry's modification time is a date without a time, and no longer crashes when the modification time is before 1970.

- Added protocol versioning between the pnpm client and pnpr server, verified applied resolution policies in resolution responses, and preserved structured error codes across the wire.

##### Performance

- Sped up `pnpm install` on macOS. On a 12-core Mac, installing 1352 packages from a warm store took 1.3 seconds, down from 2.2. pnpm now writes package files into `node_modules` with 4 threads on macOS, whatever the number of CPU cores. Set the `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS` environment variable to use a different number of threads, or to `0` to write files with the threads pnpm uses for the rest of the install.

- `pnpm install` is faster and uses less memory in large workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Each project's install no longer reads the manifests of every other workspace project again. Installs that wait for their workspace dependencies now count toward `workspaceConcurrency` [#​16966](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16966).

- Sped up workspace project discovery, dependency resolution, lockfile up-to-date checks, and peer dependency checks in large workspaces [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839) [pnpm/tasks#9](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/9). On a workspace with 6,833 projects, the lockfile up-to-date check uses about 1 second less CPU time. The peer dependency check at the end of an install now checks linked workspace projects against the manifests already in memory, without reading each `package.json` again.

- Sped up bin linking and build planning during `pnpm install`. Package binary targets and shebang runtimes are now precalculated during tarball extraction and served in `pnpr` registry metadata alongside verified `requiresBuild`, tarball size, and file-count metadata.

- Lowered peak memory when pnpm downloads many packuments, such as during lockfile verification with `trustPolicy` on Linux. In one 1,800-entry workspace, a lockfile update now peaks at 1.8 to 2.0 GB. It peaked at 2.6 to 3.7 GB before [#​17020](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17020).

- `pnpm install` in a Cargo workspace skips crates that an earlier install already unpacked into the store. Before, a repeat install processed every crate in `Cargo.lock` again. `pnpm install --force` unpacks every crate again [pnpm/tasks#69](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/69).

##### Linking node_modules and workspaces

- Concurrent installs that import the same package into one project now all complete. One of them used to fail with `ENOTEMPTY` when its copy of the package collided with the copy another install had already placed [pnpm/tasks#48](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/48).

- `pnpm install` now succeeds when `node_modules` is a symlink to an existing directory. Dependency hoisting previously rejected a symlinked `node_modules` as an invalid destination [#​17157](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17157).

- A filtered first install under the isolated linker now links every workspace project by name into `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules`, not only the selected ones [pnpm/tasks#155](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/155).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install such as `pnpm --filter app add <pkg>` keeps the root `node_modules` links and bins of the workspace projects it did not select. A project with no dependencies of its own lost them until the next full install.

- `pnpm install --filter` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `--prod` or `--dev` now preserves previously installed dependency groups for unselected workspace projects [pnpm/tasks#164](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/164). Repeat filtered installs also re-resolve when a transitive injected workspace dependency or a linked dependency's version changes.

- With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the workspace root's pnpmfile for every project, after the project's own pnpmfile. Before, it ran only the pnpmfile in the project's directory.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` now detect peer dependency issues and report linked package versions in linked projects that use `package.json5` or `package.yaml` [pnpm/tasks#172](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/172).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` no longer report an unmet peer when a workspace package's peer is provided by a remote tarball URL. pnpm now compares the peer range with the version in the tarball's manifest [#​17037](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17037).

- `pnpm prune` now removes extraneous direct packages from `node_modules` when `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are already in sync. `pnpm prune` also honors `--filter`, `--recursive`, `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, and the `trustLockfile` setting and `--trust-lockfile` flag. With the lockfile trusted, `pnpm prune --prod` works offline when every package is in the store [#​16999](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16999).

##### Injected workspace packages

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when a local directory dependency or injected workspace package changes a dependency to a different tarball URL or git commit [#​17129](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17129). It also fails when an injected workspace package changes a dependency's named-registry range, such as `work:^2.0.0`, to one the locked version no longer satisfies.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote for a `file:` dependency on a directory without a `package.json`. It also accepts the lockfile for an injected workspace package that bundles a dependency in `bundledDependencies`, lists a dependency in both `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies`, or publishes from a `publishConfig.directory` whose `package.json` lists other dependencies than the project's own. Before, these failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- The lockfile now records a `catalog:` peer dependency of an injected workspace package as written in its `package.json`. It recorded the catalog's range before, so editing the catalog changed the consumer's lockfile entry [pnpm/tasks#153](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/153).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a git, tarball, or tag dependency of an injected workspace package again when its spec changes. Before, it kept the old version.

- Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now re-check projects that inject a modified workspace package, including when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [#​17007](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17007), and accept aliased `workspace:` ranges on linked dependencies.

- An injected workspace package that was linked now becomes a copy when the project that depends on it starts providing one of its peers at a version the package's own workspace context lacks. The link used to stay until that dependency was updated, so the package could not find the peer the project provides [#​17057](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17057).

- An injected workspace package now keeps only the files its manifest lists after a lifecycle script or a script named in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` rebuilds it. Before, these refreshes copied every file of the package directory into the injected copy, including files that `files` or `.npmignore` leave out. With `deployAllFiles: true` the copy still gets every file.

- A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` now keeps a package's links to its own files as links in the injected copies, the way `pnpm install` writes them, and updates those copies when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. Before, a directory link the script added became a real directory or went missing with `deployAllFiles`, and with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` the copies kept the files from the last install.

##### Running scripts and checking dependencies

- Pressing Ctrl+C during `pnpm -r run` or `pnpm --filter <pkg> run` no longer reports 

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ✂ PR body was truncated to here.


</details>

### Configuration and setting up pnpm

- Registry credentials and TLS settings passed with `--config`, such as `--config.//registry.example.com/:_authToken=<token>`, are now applied. They take precedence over the same settings in `.npmrc` files.

- pnpm now reads only the settings it needs to decide whether to switch to the pnpm version a project pins. A setting outside them can no longer fail that decision or change its outcome. For example, `pnpm --version` no longer fails in a pinned project whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a setting this pnpm cannot read. Projects that pin neither pnpm nor a runtime skip this check without reading any settings.

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, an option only the pinned pnpm knows now reaches that pnpm when it comes immediately before the command name, as in `pnpm --new-flag install`. When switching for `pnpm --version` or an unrecognized command line, pnpm also honors `--color`, `--no-color`, `--reporter`, and `--loglevel` wherever they appear on the command line.

- `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it, leaving the global pnpm alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). Run inside a workspace package, `pnpm self-update` updates the pin in the workspace root's manifest, including in `package.yaml` or `package.json5`.

- `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167).

- `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973).

- In StackBlitz WebContainers, `pnpm` no longer crashes intermittently with `Parking not supported on this platform`, and running a command that does not exist now reports that the command was not found. Previously it sometimes failed with a generic error.

### [`v12.14.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.14.0): pnpm 12.14.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.13.0...v12.14.0)

This release adds the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting, stops `pnpm install` from waiting on the daily update check, and keeps pnpm from aborting with a core dump when the reader of its output exits.

##### Minor Changes

- Added the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build depends on something pnpm cannot include in the cache key, such as the system libraries a native addon links against. pnpm builds the listed packages in every project and never restores or saves their builds through the side-effects cache, locally or on a `remoteCache` server. Under the global virtual store, each project gets its own copy of these packages and of the packages that depend on them. Entries use the same `name`, `@scope/*`, and `name@version` patterns as `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#​5271](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5271).

- `pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header during web-based login. Registries use it to show the verification code that completes the sign-in in the browser.

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` no longer wait for the daily update check. If the command finishes first, pnpm skips the update notice and checks again next time. On a registry that accepted the connection but never answered, an install that had nothing to do used to take minutes [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839).

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` now reuse `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the workspace configures a catalog entry that no dependency references, such as an unused entry or one whose package an `overrides` entry replaces. Before, every resolution in such a workspace resolved all dependencies again from the registry [#​16923](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16923).

- `pnpm install` now looks up a git dependency's branch or tag once per install, even when many workspace projects depend on it. With `linkWorkspacePackages` enabled, it used to run `git ls-remote` once per project [#​16899](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16899).

- A filtered install, such as `pnpm install --filter <pkg>`, now keeps the `pnpm-lock.yaml` entries of workspace projects that are missing from disk, as in a sparse checkout. Their importers, packages, and catalog entries stay even when the filter matches every project on disk [#​16931](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16931).

- pnpm now decides whether a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer is linked as a dependency or as a peer from the shallowest path that reaches the package. When an existing lockfile records such a dependency as a regular dependency and a newly added dependency now provides the peer, pnpm records it as a peer, as a fresh install does. The lockfile entry of such a package can change on the next install [#​16901](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901).

- An install that adds nothing to the store no longer changes the modification time of the store directory. CI caches that check modification times, such as GitLab's, no longer re-upload an unchanged store [#​16929](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16929).

##### Running commands and scripts

- pnpm no longer aborts with a core dump when the reader of its output has exited, as in `pnpm list | head -1` or `pnpm start 2>&1 | head -1`. The command finishes with its usual exit code, and a failing script's exit code is kept. A write to stdout that fails for another reason, such as a full disk, ends the command with exit code 1 [#​16904](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16904) [pnpm/tasks#132](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/132).

- On Windows, `pnpm exec`, `pnpm run`, and commands such as `pnpm nx` now return when the command they run exits, even if it left a detached process running and pnpm's output is redirected or piped. Previously a shell reading that output waited until the detached process, such as the Nx daemon, exited [#​16930](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16930).

- Commands that do not write the project manifest now leave a missing `package.json` absent. This covers queries such as `pnpm why` and `pnpm outdated`, `pnpm fetch`, `pnpm dedupe --check`, and commands that exit with an error, such as `pnpm rt ls`. These commands used to create one from the initialization template. `pnpm sbom` run from a lockfile alone now reports the root component as `unknown` with version `0.0.0` [#​16907](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16907).

- `pnpm run` now reports a failed script as a JSON record under `--reporter=ndjson`. It printed a plain `[ELIFECYCLE]` line to stderr.

- `pnpm run` no longer prints `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code N.` to stderr when a script fails under `--reporter=silent`, `--silent`, or `--loglevel=silent`.

- `pnpm pipeline --dry-run` no longer writes a run report when no projects are selected. With `--json` it prints `{"tasks": []}` [pnpm/tasks#126](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/126).

##### Packing and publishing

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now ship the whole gitignored directory that `main`, `browser`, or `bin` points into, as npm does. Previously only the `main` and `bin` files themselves were packed, and a gitignored `browser` file was left out [#​16908](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16908).

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now honor a `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` inside a subdirectory when `package.json` has a `files` field. The package root's ignore files and those inherited from the workspace are still skipped [#​16909](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16909).

##### Setting up pnpm and toolchains

- `--registry`, `--https-proxy`, `--http-proxy`, and `--no-proxy` now apply when pnpm resolves and downloads the pnpm version a project pins in `packageManager`. Before, these lookups went to `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, which a firewall that only allows a private registry blocks [#​16911](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16911).

- On Windows, `pnpm install` now installs the Rust toolchain for rustup's default host, so a machine set up with `rustup set default-host x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` gets the MinGW toolchain. Without a default host, pnpm installs the MSVC toolchain for the machine's architecture, as rustup does. This includes a pnpm built for MinGW, such as the MSYS2 package, which has installed the MinGW toolchain since 12.13.0. An x64 pnpm on ARM64 Windows now installs the ARM64 toolchain [#​16854](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16854).

### [`v12.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.13.0): pnpm 12.13.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.12.1...v12.13.0)

This release adds the `pnpm profile` and `pnpm token` commands, the `storeIndexFormat: files` setting for stores shared over a network filesystem, and faster Python dependency resolution.

##### Minor Changes

- Added the `pnpm profile` command to view and update registry user profile settings.

- Added `pnpm token` to list, create, and revoke authentication tokens on the registry.

- Added the `storeIndexFormat` setting. Set it to `files` to keep a store's package index as one file per package instead of the SQLite `index.db`, for a store on a network filesystem that several machines use at once. SQLite's locking does not work across machines, so concurrent installs on such a store could corrupt `index.db`.

- Added the `nodePackageMap` setting, which groups the package-map settings. `nodePackageMap.mode: write-only` writes `node_modules/.package-map.json` for other tools without making Node.js load it. `mode: load` also makes Node.js load the map, like `nodeExperimentalPackageMap: true`. `nodePackageMap.type` replaces `nodePackageMapType`. The old settings still work [#​14937](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14937).

  ```yaml
  nodePackageMap:
    mode: write-only
    type: loose
  ```

##### Patch Changes

##### Setting up pnpm

- `pnpm setup` now works when pnpm was installed with npm on macOS. It installed pnpm from npm's `bin` directory and left a `$PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm` that could not run [#​16855](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16855).

- pnpm runs again after `pnpm setup` when `globalShims` enables pnpm. Every command failed with "the global target of the pnpm shim points back at the shim" [#​16874](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16874).

- A pnpm built for the MinGW target on Windows, such as the MSYS2 package, now installs the MinGW Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. It used to install the MSVC toolchain.

##### Installing packages

- On macOS, `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_WRITE_FILE` when the project is on a virtiofs or SMB share. pnpm now falls back to a regular `fsync` when the file system rejects a full sync [#​16846](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16846).

- On macOS, `pnpm install`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and other commands that load a pnpmfile no longer hang at random.

- `pnpm install` now puts the executables of a Python build backend's requirements on the `PATH` while the backend runs. Projects built with `uv_build` now install. Before, they failed with "uv-build was not properly installed".

- Removing a `link:` dependency now also removes its symlink from `node_modules` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​16884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884).

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` no longer records the tarball URL of a package installed from a scoped registry, such as one set by `@types:registry=`, when pnpm can rebuild the URL from that registry [#​16866](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16866).

##### Packing, auditing, and pipelines

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now pack only `package.json`, the README, the license, and the files named in `main` and `bin` when `files` is an empty array. They used to pack every file in the package [#​16889](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16889).

- `pnpm audit` and `pnpm audit signatures` no longer check runtimes installed through `devEngines.runtime`, such as `node@runtime:24.21.0`, against the npm package of the same name. `pnpm audit signatures` reported these runtimes as having an invalid registry signature [#​16869](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16869).

- `pnpm pipeline` now runs the root's tasks when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists only the root in `packages` or omits `packages`, as `pnpm -r run` does. A change to a root file in such a workspace no longer triggers a full-run warning. When a full run has no projects to run, `pnpm pipeline` now reports that no projects are selected [#​16849](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16849).

##### Performance

- `pnpm install` resolves Python dependencies faster. With `--lockfile-only`, a project with 10 dependencies now resolves in about 4 seconds, down from about 40. When the index publishes a metadata file beside each wheel (PEP 658), as PyPI does, pnpm downloads only the wheels of the releases it selects.

- A repeat install against an existing lockfile no longer reads registry metadata for the dependencies it takes from that lockfile. On a warm store this removes thousands of metadata lookups from a repeat install of a large workspace.

- `pnpm install` with `enableModulesDir: false` now verifies the packages already in the store while the dependencies resolve, and checks a package's files in parallel. On a 5,100-package install with the store on a network filesystem, this removed a 19-second pause between resolution and fetching.
